sections.title: Overview
sections.body: The What-If Simulator lets Controllers, Executives, CC Owners, and Project Leads model hypothetical portfolio scenarios without affecting live data. It operates in three phases: Scenario Manager (browse / create), Scenario Workspace (build and analyze), and Comparison View (side-by-side analysis). Project Leads can author scenarios scoped to their own projects and apply published scenarios to their own forecast (see Apply to Forecast).

sections.title: Scenario Manager
sections.body: The landing view shows your saved scenarios and published scenarios from others. Each scenario card shows its name, author, status (private / published), tags, and headline impact. Create a new scenario from scratch or clone an existing one. Delete scenarios you own. Publish scenarios to make them visible to other users (subject to Tier 3 gating — see below). Archive scenarios that have served their purpose; archived scenarios are hidden by default but visible under the Show archived filter.

sections.title: Scenario Workspace
sections.body: The workspace has a split layout: an action panel on the left and an impact dashboard on the right. Add actions to model changes, and the impact dashboard updates immediately with the recalculated results. Nine dimension tiles populate after recalculation: Financial / Ranking / Capacity / People / Outsourcing / Investment Mix / Running Cost / Cost Allocation / Change Summary. The header shows the last-recalculated indicator (e.g. 'Recalculated 36d ago') and a Stale flag if the anchor ForecastVersion has been superseded — use the Rebase action in the ⋯ menu to re-anchor.

sections.title: Editing surfaces: project scope vs portfolio scope
sections.body:
**Project scope — WYSIWYG editable forecast grid (primary surface)**

At project scope the simulator is directly editable. Open a project from the workspace left rail and work with the grid exactly as you do in the Workbench forecast cycle:
- Edit forecast cells directly — hours on internal role lines, € on external-cost lines. Future cells are editable; actuals are read-only. Hours are converted to € at the RateTable rate **in force at that cell's month** (rate-at-month lookup, not the latest rate) — so a rate step mid-year prices later months at the new rate, re-typing the same hours leaves € unchanged, and the grid always agrees with what Promote writes. Internal role lines are split **by workforce location** (Munich / Budapest / Pune) so that staffing at different locations is shown as separate rows, each priced at its location's rate.
- Add or remove role lines.
- Add, remove, or edit external-cost line items (vendor, category, description).
- Adjust project start/end dates — the grid reflects the shifted window.
- Edit pipeline stage, DoI, and milestones.
- Change the seniority/sourcing mix (Tier-3 authors only — the mix control is not rendered for non-Tier-3 users).

A **macro strip** above the grid provides four configurable bulk operations for edits that are tedious to do cell-by-cell:
1. **Delay by N months** — shifts the project start, end, and every forecast cell N months later, preserving the curve shape and total.
2. **Accelerate by N months** — the mirror of delay; pulls everything N months earlier (clamped so the project cannot move earlier than the current open forecast month).
3. **Pause for N months** — suspends the project; the remaining curve resumes after the pause.
4. **Remove** — removes the project from the scenario's portfolio for impact purposes.

Macros and direct cell edits coexist: macros are the coarse tool; the grid is the scalpel. Direct edits always win over macro-shifted values for the cells they touch.

**Portfolio scope — configurable bulk-lever catalogue (unchanged)**

At portfolio scope a fixed catalogue of bulk actions remains the right tool because dozens of projects move at once. These levers are unchanged: Across-the-Board Cut (percentage reduction on all projects), Cut by LoB (target a specific organisational entity), Cut by Type (target CapEx or OpEx), Freeze New Starts (prevent planned projects from beginning), Cap Cost Category (limit a specific cost type), and Rate Escalation (model hourly rate increases).

Tech Navigator profile edits (edit a project's TN sub-criteria; composite recomputes against scenario weights) also remain available.

Levers touching `cost_allocation` flag `tier3_content_flag=true` and require Tier 3 visibility for publish + promote per `[F-AC-01]`.

sections.title: Cost-allocation sandbox (Stage 1 + Stage 2)
sections.body:
The cost-allocation sandbox is the simulator's fully editable surface for modelling changes to the two-stage cost flow before committing them to canonical state. It covers both Stage 1 inter-service distribution edges and Stage 2 BTC profile lines. This is the `lever_category='cost_allocation'` surface (Tier 3).

**What is editable:**
- Stage 1 distribution edges — edit percentages, delete destinations, and **add new destinations** (the sandbox fully supports adding a new Stage 1 destination that does not exist in the canonical version).
- Stage 2 BTC profile lines — the full BTC line set is editable; percentages can be freely adjusted as long as they sum to 100.
- `to_business_pct` on the entity.

**Isolation — canonical state is never touched:**
- Stage 1 edges fork into a dedicated per-scenario `DistributionVersion` (`scenario_id=N`, `status='draft'` permanently) on first mutation; the production version's edges are never mutated.
- Stage 2 BTC line edits live as `ScenarioAction` overlays; canonical `BTCProfile` / `BTCProfileLine` rows are untouched until Promote.

**Sandbox UI**: in the scenario workspace, navigate to the **Cost Allocation Sandbox** surface (Bulk Actions → Cost Allocation). The same Charging editors mount here in sandbox mode — UM refresh and mode-switch buttons are hidden by design (canonical-only operations); a blue 'Sandbox edit' chip indicates the mode.

**Impact preview**: the right-side Cost Allocation dimension tile shows headline numbers (e.g. 'Rebalances ~€283k of annual Stage-2 charge from DE legal entity to PL+CZ legal entities'). The embedded RollupView mounts in compact + scenario-version mode for visual diff.

**Promote**: the ⋯ menu's Promote action materialises overlays onto canonical rows. Permission per `[F-AC-01]`: controllers always allowed; other roles need an explicit `RolePermissionGrant`. Audit trail: each Promote click creates a `ScenarioPromotion` row with `routing_summary_json` listing per-action routing, status, and target.

sections.title: Tier 3 Visibility Gating
sections.body:
Per `[B-SL-03]`, scenarios containing cost-allocation edits (Stage 1 distribution edge changes or Stage 2 BTC line changes) auto-set `tier3_content_flag=true`. Three visibility levels:
- `private` — author only
- `tier3_only` — Tier 3 users (those with `tier3_flag=true` on their User row)
- `all_users` — anyone authenticated

**Publish gating**: trying to publish a Tier 3 scenario without `tier3_flag` is blocked with 'Tier 3 publish requires elevated permissions'. Promoting a Tier 3 scenario requires both `tier3_flag=true` AND a `RolePermissionGrant` for the relevant `entity_type` (`btc_profile` or `distribution`). Controllers default-have these grants; other roles need explicit admin-issued grants per `[F-AC-01]`.

**Example**: 'MDH BTC Rebalance — DE/PL/CZ' is a Tier 3 scenario authored by Anna Meier. Publishing it as `tier3_only` makes it visible to other Tier 3 users; promoting it materialises BTC line shifts onto the live `off-mdh` profile.

sections.title: Apply to Forecast (PL flow)
sections.body:
Project Leads can pre-populate their next forecast cycle from two routes:

**From a PL-authored scenario (own projects):** If you have authored a scenario scoped to your own projects, open it in the workspace and click **Apply to forecast** in the page header. The modal confirms which of your projects will have diffs pre-loaded.

**From a published scenario (leadership handoff):** When a published scenario contains diffs that affect a project you lead, the simulator presents only your slice — not the full strategic scenario. Locate the published scenario, click the row (workspace opens read-only for scenarios you do not own), and click **Apply to forecast**.

In both cases, clicking **Confirm apply** creates draft Change Requests (one per cost centre per affected project) grouped by cost centre. These appear in your **Change History** in the Workbench where you can review and refine them before submitting into the normal CR approval workflow. A result panel shows how many draft CRs were created and offers a link to review them. Re-applying the same scenario replaces your prior draft CRs from that scenario, so you can easily update your pre-populated changes if the scenario is revised.

sections.title: Actions
sections.body:
Actions target either individual projects (project scope) or the entire portfolio (portfolio scope).

**Project scope — WYSIWYG direct editing:** At project scope the primary surface is the directly-editable forecast grid. You edit cells, add and remove role lines, edit external-cost line items, adjust milestones/DoI/stage, and move project dates directly. The macro strip provides four bulk helpers: Delay by N months, Accelerate by N months, Pause for N months, and Remove. The old discrete project-scope action forms (Reduce/Adjust Budget, Increase Budget, Cut Consulting, Adjust External Cost) are retired as inputs — that editing is now done directly in the grid.

**Portfolio scope — bulk lever catalogue:** Across-the-Board Cut (percentage reduction on all projects), Cut by LoB (target a specific organisational entity), Cut by Type (target CapEx or OpEx), Freeze New Starts (prevent planned projects from beginning), Cap Cost Category (limit a specific cost type), and Rate Escalation (model hourly rate increases). These remain form-driven at portfolio scope where bulk edits are the right paradigm.

**Tech Navigator edits:** Edit a project's TN sub-criteria within the scenario; the composite recomputes against the scenario weights, allowing the user to model 'what if Project X had a different scoring profile'.

Every edit triggers a server-side recompute and returns the full recalculated scenario state.

sections.title: Impact Dashboard (9 dimensions)
sections.body:
Shows the cascading effects of all applied actions across nine dimensions:
- **Financial** — total budget delta, capex/opex split, savings target tracking
- **Ranking** — Backlog cutoff impact, cutoff line shift
- **Capacity** — FTE delta per CC, utilisation shifts
- **People** — over/under-allocated count by role
- **Outsourcing** — internal vs external mix
- **Investment Mix** — by hierarchy node / by type / by RAG band
- **Running Cost** — Run Portfolio impact (DoI 5 entities)
- **Cost Allocation** — Stage 1 + Stage 2 deltas (cost-allocation sandbox edits only)
- **Change Summary** — flat list of every action with categorisation

Drill down into any metric to see project-level detail.

sections.title: Comparison View
sections.body: Select 2–5 scenarios to compare side-by-side. The comparison shows key metrics (budget, timeline, capacity, RAG changes) for each scenario in parallel columns. The first column always shows the **Current State** as a baseline for comparison. Click any scenario card in the comparison to drill into its full workspace.

sections.title: AI Advisor
sections.body:
The AI Advisor panel (top-right of the workspace) lets you describe a goal in natural language — for example, 'Find 2M in savings' or 'Get all teams below 95% utilization'. The system matches your goal to pre-computed solution paths and presents 2–3 options with different trade-offs. Select a path to apply its constituent actions to your scenario.

**Seeded goals (5 in v5)**:
- *Find approximately 2M in savings* (Conservative / Moderate / Aggressive)
- *Get all teams below 95% utilization* (Redistribute / Defer)
- *Prioritize Rail Systems investments* (Accelerate / Balanced)
- *Eliminate Red RAG projects* (Fund It / Reduce Scope)
- *Rebalance Master Data Hub BTC across DE/PL/CZ* (DE→PL/CZ split / DE→broader EMEA) — cost-allocation sandbox demo

If no pattern matches, the advisor returns a friendly hint listing the available goal areas. With `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` set in Planning Parameters, the advisor can also engage in dynamic Claude-powered conversations.

sections.title: CC-Owner-scoped scenarios
sections.body: Per `[F-AC-01]`, when a CC Owner (e.g. Thomas Brenner) creates a scenario, the scenario is automatically scoped to `cc_owner_scope_cc_id=<their CC>`. The scenario is only visible to that CC's owners + controllers; published CC-scoped scenarios surface under the recipient's Published list with a CC chip. CC-scoped scenarios cannot be promoted by their author — promotion still requires the controller's permission grant for the relevant entity type.

sections.title: Promote (Forecast)
sections.body: When a scenario contains forecast changes to a project you do not own, promoting the scenario creates draft Change Requests for that project's owner. The draft CRs appear in the owning Project Lead's Change History in the Workbench, ready for review and refinement before submission into the normal CR workflow. This keeps the owning PL informed and in control of changes that affect their projects.

sections.title: Important Notes
sections.body: Scenarios are sandboxes — they never affect live portfolio data unless promoted (cost-allocation edits and forecast diffs across to other PLs' draft CRs) or applied-to-forecast (PL flow). All impact calculations are performed server-side. Pre-built scenarios use pre-computed snapshots for instant loading. The AI Advisor uses pattern matching by default and Claude when API key is configured. All charts and visualizations support both light and dark mode themes. Scenario delete cleanup removes scenario-version Distribution rows and BTC overlays per `services/scenario_cost_allocation.cleanup_cost_allocation_state`.
